responses.content:
The statement is incorrect. The invention of the telephone is credited to Alexander Graham Bell, a Scottish-born inventor and scientist.

Alexander Graham Bell patented the first practical telephone on March 7, 1876, at his laboratory in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. He developed the first device that could transmit the human voice over wires, revolutionizing communication forever.

Paris was indeed where he conducted many of his experiments, but it's not associated with the invention of the telephone.
